option_relations.rationale: Ascending aortic aneurysm with thrombus formation complicating coronary perfusion is a manifestation or a description of the clinical scenario that leads to Aortic Valve Thrombosis with Coronary Artery Occlusion.

Bicuspid aortic valve with ascending aortic aneurysm and valvular thrombosis describes the underlying conditions and findings that contribute to Aortic Valve Thrombosis with Coronary Artery Occlusion.

Organized thrombus formation on native bicuspid aortic valve with ascending aortic aneurysm is essentially equivalent to Aortic Valve Thrombosis with Coronary Artery Occlusion, as the thrombus on the valve is causing the occlusion.
Bicuspid aortic valve with thrombus-induced coronary ostial obstruction describes a key component and consequence of Aortic Valve Thrombosis with Coronary Artery Occlusion.
